title: SessionView
description: One of the caller's own sessions, as the user sees it in their own list, derived from identity_application::sessions::SessionView. Note what is ABSENT: no secret, no token, no hash, no cookie value, no security_version. The session_id is a handle, not a credential — knowing it is not enough to authenticate, because the transport also carries a secret the server stores hashed. The administrative view of a user's sessions is a different type (UserSessionSummary), reached through a different trait that takes a user_id.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; ListSessionsQuery has no body and no route serves it

session_id.description: The session's identifier. A transparent newtype over a UUID in Rust. A handle, not a credential: presenting it is not authentication.

created_at_ms.description: When it was created, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. A signed 64-bit integer in Rust; negative values are representable and are not meaningful dates.

expires_at_ms.description: When it expires, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Absolute, not a duration: a duration stored on the row would make 'when does this expire' depend on when you asked. The domain refuses to construct a session whose expiry does not follow its creation.

aal.description: The assurance level the session was ESTABLISHED at. Distinct from whether a step-up happened later: Aal is a floor for the session's lifetime, while a step-up is a property of a moment.

x-accepted-values.constraining: an enum in Rust; wire values "aal1" | "aal2", matching Aal::as_wire()

label.description: A COARSE label for where the session came from. Never a user-agent string stored verbatim: it is displayed in a list an account-takeover attacker will be reading, and an unescaped user-agent is a stored-XSS vector. Serialised as null when absent, not omitted.
label.x-serde-note: Option<String> with no skip_serializing_if, so the key is always present.

current.description: Whether this session is the one making the request. The current session is marked so the UI can offer 'this device' separately. Client-computed from the request context, not a stored column.

x-omission-rule.rule: every field is always present. `label` is the only nullable one.
x-omission-rule.test: identity_application::sessions::tests::a_session_view_exposes_no_secret_material asserts the serialised view contains no 'secret', 'token', 'hash', 'cookie' or 'security_version'
